name: Trifluridine/tipiracil
drug_class: Thymidine-based nucleoside analogue with thymidine phosphorylase inhibitor
mechanism: Trifluridine is incorporated into DNA and disrupts DNA function. Tipiracil inhibits thymidine phosphorylase, increasing systemic exposure to trifluridine.

name: Fluorouracil
mechanism: Intracellular metabolites inhibit thymidylate synthase and can be incorporated into RNA and DNA, disrupting nucleic-acid synthesis and function.

name: Folinic acid
mechanism: Stabilises the fluorouracil–thymidylate synthase complex, enhancing fluorouracil-mediated inhibition of thymidylate synthesis. It is not itself a cytotoxic component in these regimens.

name: Oxaliplatin
mechanism: Forms platinum–DNA adducts and cross-links that interfere with DNA replication and transcription, leading to cell death.

name: Irinotecan
mechanism: Its active metabolite SN-38 stabilises the topoisomerase I–DNA complex, preventing repair of single-strand breaks during DNA replication.

name: Durvalumab
mechanism: Binds PD-L1 and blocks its interaction with PD-1 and CD80, supporting restoration of antitumour T-cell activity.

name: Pembrolizumab
mechanism: Binds PD-1 and blocks interaction with PD-L1 and PD-L2, reducing inhibitory signalling in activated T cells.

name: Nivolumab
mechanism: Binds PD-1 and blocks ligand-mediated inhibitory signalling, supporting antitumour T-cell responses.

name: Atezolizumab
mechanism: Binds PD-L1 and blocks interactions with PD-1 and CD80, reducing checkpoint-mediated suppression of T-cell activity.

name: Pemetrexed
mechanism: Inhibits folate-dependent enzymes involved in purine and thymidylate synthesis, impairing DNA and RNA synthesis.

name: Carboplatin
mechanism: Forms platinum–DNA adducts and cross-links that disrupt DNA replication and transcription.

name: Paclitaxel
mechanism: Promotes microtubule assembly and prevents normal microtubule disassembly, disrupting mitosis and intracellular transport.

name: Docetaxel
mechanism: Stabilises microtubules and inhibits their depolymerisation, causing disruption of mitotic and cellular functions.

name: Doxorubicin
mechanism: Intercalates into DNA, inhibits topoisomerase II and generates reactive species, causing DNA damage and impaired replication.

name: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin
mechanism: Delivers doxorubicin in a pegylated liposomal formulation. Released doxorubicin intercalates DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II.

name: Cyclophosphamide
mechanism: Hepatic activation produces metabolites that form DNA cross-links, interfering with DNA replication and cell division.

name: Trastuzumab
mechanism: Binds the extracellular domain of HER2, inhibiting signalling and promoting immune-mediated destruction of HER2-expressing tumour cells.

name: Pertuzumab
mechanism: Binds a different extracellular HER2 domain from trastuzumab and inhibits ligand-dependent HER2 dimerisation with other HER family receptors.

name: Abemaciclib
mechanism: Inhibits cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6, reducing retinoblastoma-protein phosphorylation and limiting progression from G1 to S phase.

name: Bevacizumab
mechanism: Binds VEGF-A and reduces activation of VEGF receptors, inhibiting tumour-associated angiogenic signalling.

name: Gemcitabine
mechanism: Active metabolites inhibit ribonucleotide reductase and are incorporated into DNA, impairing DNA synthesis.

name: Cisplatin
mechanism: Forms intra- and inter-strand DNA cross-links that disrupt DNA replication and transcription.

name: Axitinib
mechanism: Inhibits VEGFR-1, VEGFR-2 and VEGFR-3 signalling, reducing angiogenesis and tumour vascular growth.

name: Enfortumab vedotin
drug_class: Nectin-4-directed antibody linked to a microtubule-disrupting payload
mechanism: Binds Nectin-4, is internalised and releases monomethyl auristatin E, which disrupts microtubules and induces cell death.
